overall: The AG found no violation for failing to periodically review pre-July 2010 minutes, but found violations for withholding minutes after their purpose expired, four roll-call and four document-listing lapses, and thin minutes in 29 sets; it ordered release and amendments.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to timely produce 2008-2009 executive session minutes after a request.
allegations.key_passage: This allegation was addressed in OML 2014-105.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee did not announce its determination that continued non-disclosure of 2008-2009 minutes was warranted, as required by periodic review.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by failing to periodically review executive session minutes from meetings held prior to July 1, 2010.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to periodically review executive session minutes from 2005-2014, so minutes were withheld after their purpose expired.
allegations.key_passage: by failing to periodically review executive session minutes and release those that no longer needed to be withheld;

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the redacted portions of 2008-2009 executive session minutes (collective bargaining and non-union contracts) should be disclosed.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the executive session purpose has expired, thus the Committee may no longer withhold these minutes under the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant challenged continued redaction of January 31, 2011 and December 2, 2013 executive session minutes on collective bargaining strategy.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the executive session purpose has expired with respect to these minutes as well, and the public interest in transparency outweighs the potential for harm to the Committee's future bargaining position.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to take votes by roll call during 2008-2009 executive sessions.
allegations.key_passage: Because the alleged violations occurred prior to the date our office assumed jurisdiction over local public bodies, we decline to review the complaint.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to take and record roll call votes in four executive sessions.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, while the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law in this respect, we believe it is now aware of its responsibility to record all executive session votes as roll call votes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged minutes of five executive sessions failed to list documents used; committee conceded four and disputed one.
allegations.key_passage: While we find a violation with respect to these four sets of minutes, we credit the Committee's response with regard to the May 30, 2013 meeting and find no violation there.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the May 30, 2013 executive session minutes failed to list a document used during that meeting.
allegations.key_passage: we credit the Committee's response with regard to the May 30, 2013 meeting and find no violation there.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged 29 sets of executive session minutes lacked enough detail for a non-attendee to understand what occurred.
allegations.key_passage: and by failing to provide sufficient detail in 29 sets of executive session minutes.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law; the Committee was cautioned that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intentional violation.
Publicly release the executive session minutes of its 2008, 2009, January 31, 2011, and December 2, 2013 meetings, subject to attorney-client privilege and Public Records Law exemptions.
Review and amend its January 31, 2011 and January 14, 2013 meeting minutes to include the documents used during those executive sessions, if not already done.

Amend the minutes of the October 12, 2010, January 31, 2011, September 24, 2012, and March 10, 2014 meetings to include information about any roll call votes taken on those dates, to the best of its ability.
remedy_passage: The Committee must take all of these remedial actions within sixty (60) days of receipt of this letter.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
